article.headline: Tessa Johnson's career-high 32 points lifts No. 1 South Carolina to 65-56 win over No. 7 UConn
article.description: — Tessa Johnson scored a career-high 32 points and No. 1 South Carolina shut down seventh-ranked UConn's offense in a 65-56 victory Tuesday night in the Basketball Hall of Fame Women's Showcase.
article.linkText: Tessa Johnson's career-high 32 points lifts No. 1 South Carolina to 65-56 win over No. 7 UConn
article.story: UNCASVILLE, Conn. -- — Tessa Johnson scored a career-high 32 points and No. 1 South Carolina shut down seventh-ranked UConn's offense in a 65-56 victory Tuesday night in the Basketball Hall of Fame Women's Showcase. The game was a rematch of last season's national semifinal that the Gamecocks won and was marred by a heated exchange between UConn coach Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley just before the final buzzer. The two Hall of Famers exchanged a quick handshake pregame and the Huskies (4-3) jumped out to a quick 7-0 lead. The advantage didn't last long as the Gamecocks rallied without leading scorer Joyce Edwards, who was out with an illness. Trailing 20-16 midway through the second quarter, South Carolina (7-0) took control of the game. The Gamecocks scored 22 of the final 24 points in the half, including the last 16. Agot Makeer had a four-point play with 3 seconds left to make it 38-22. That was about the only good offensive stretch for either team. South Carolina used its defense to hold UConn to just 27% shooting for the game, including 24% in the second half. Trailing by double-digits for most of the second half, the Huskies were able to get within 54-46 midway through the fourth quarter, but Johnson answered with two straight baskets to restore the double-digit lead and end any hope of a UConn comeback. Sarah Strong had 22 points and 12 rebounds to lead the Huskies. The loss was only the second ever for UConn at Mohegan Sun. The Huskies were 49-1 all-time at the arena, with the only other defeat coming in 2021 in this event against Louisville. UConn was without guards KK Arnold and Kayleigh Heckel. Arnold had a lower body injury and Heckel has a back issue. The Huskies have now played five games against Top 25 opponents and have a few more on the horizon over the next few weeks. South Carolina has played its own gauntlet of a schedule. The Gamecocks have faced four Top 25 opponents so far and the game against UConn starts a stretch of five ranked matchups in the team’s next eight contests. Up next South Carolina: Hosts Tennessee State on Saturday. UConn: Plays No. 5 Duke on Saturday in Boston. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college basketball coverage here
